thread:
maria SRE: FYI — we started getting multiple customer tickets about much higher inference tail latency around 06:12 UTC. p95 up ~2x, p99 up ~4x for hosted text-gen. Spike appears correlated with this morning's node image rollout (kernel 6.4.3 -> 6.5.0 + GPU firmware v2.14). :frowning:

alex (eng-runtime): reported from observability — CPU sys% and iowait both spike on affected hosts. Token-level traces show long stalls during KV cache lookup, but redis latency is normal. Notable: kernel dmesg shows repeated nvme controller reset messages.

tariq (eng-infra): iostat and nvme-cli confirm high average completion latency on nvme0 across affected hosts. We have a small canary pool with the new image that rolled at 06:05, matches timeframe.

jen (support): Several customers opened high-sev tickets describing "sudden latency jumps" and "timeouts on p99 requests". I pushed a proactive note to customers in the affected orgs and asked them to forward samples — will paste snippets here when I have them.

maria SRE: quick repro steps from oncall: spin up a small inference job (t5-small-ish), run steady 50 qps with concurrent streams and measure tail. On affected hosts we see single-request latencies mostly fine but occasional 700ms-1.2s tails. Root cause hypothesis: new kernel introduces different NVMe IO scheduler behavior under heavy small-writes (checkpoint/writeback from CUDA unified memory) and combined with GPU firmware change that affects DMA ordering, causing stalls.

kai (eng-sre): ran perf + eBPF to sample syscall stacks during stalls. Stack collapsed to kernel block layer and nvme_rw path. eBPF trace snippet below:

```
# eBPF sample (abridged) during stall
nvme_submit -> nvme_queue_rq -> blk_mq_dispatch_rq -> __blk_mq_make_request -> io_schedule -> __schedule
# userspace callers: torch::cuda::Allocator::alloc -> inference_loop -> network_send
```

alex (eng-runtime): also saw many threads stuck in `__blk_mq_run_hw_queue` with `nvme_do_request` waiting for completions. nvidia-smi dmon doesn't show abnormal GPU utilization — GPUs idle while requests back up.

tariq (eng-infra): immediate mitigations I applied to the canary pool: switched NVMe scheduler from `mq-deadline` to `noop` and disabled `writeback` for our inference temporary volume. Commands:

```
# on each affected host (canary)
echo noop > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler
mount -o remount,noauto_da_alloc /var/lib/redwood/inference_tmp || true
# reduce background writeback pressure
sysctl -w vm.dirty_ratio=5
sysctl -w vm.dirty_background_ratio=2
```

maria SRE: after that change canaries dropped p99 by ~60% within 5 minutes. Good signal that scheduler/writeback was major contributor.

jen (support): passing that update to customers helped some orgs; a few still saw intermittent spikes. They reported a known vendor firmware release note mentioning "improved DMA ordering" which could interact badly with certain kernel versions.

kai (eng-sre): we also observed a small percentage of hosts with NVMe firmware logs showing error recovery entries. nvme-cli `get-log` shows repeated error entries around 06:10. Suspect combination: kernel change altered queue depth handling, firmware GC triggered, causing long controller resets while CUDA attempted pinned-memory DMA.

alex (eng-runtime): quick runtime-side mitigation we pushed: route latency-sensitive hosted requests to a separate pool that is pinned to the previous stable node image (kernel 6.4.3 + firmware v2.13). Also enabled request-level fallback to smaller model variant for canary clients to reduce burst severity. Routing change applied via smart-routing policy:

```
route-policy add --name=kernel-rollout-fallback --match=hosted,latency_sensitive --prefer=pool:stable-6.4
```

tariq (eng-infra): next steps I'm taking now: 1) pause rollout across the fleet; 2) schedule rolling rollback for canaries to the previous image; 3) coordinate with HW vendor to get firmware telemetry and confirm if vendor-side fixes exist; 4) run focused stress test for unified memory + NVMe writeback to reproduce in lab.

maria SRE: agreed. I also want an immediate playbook entry so oncall can move faster next time. Draft mitigation checklist:
- Pause node image rollout.
- Switch NVMe scheduler to noop on canary pool.
- Reduce vm.dirty ratios temporarily.
- Route latency-sensitive traffic to stable pools.
- If NVMe errors present, isolate host and repro in infra lab; escalate to vendor.

jen (support): I updated the incident notice to affected customers, included mitigation status and ETA for rollback. Customers appreciated the routing fallback.

ops-bot: canary rollback job queued: job-id=rb-20250711-17, estimated time 12m.

maria SRE: notes for postmortem and longer-term fixes:
- Add kernel+GPU-firmware compatibility tests to pre-rollout canaries that include NVMe-heavy unified-memory workloads (we didn't run those today).
- Add NVMe firmware health checks and parse `get-log` anomalies as a rollout blocker.
- Add an infra canary that runs periodic `iostat`/`nvme-cli` checks and auto-flag if completion latency > 5ms.
- Improve automatic routing fallback so it can be enacted automatically if p99 > threshold for X minutes.

kai (eng-sre): will also add a short eBPF probe to the canary agents to surface `blk_mq` stalls in the console so we have early warning.

alex (eng-runtime): follow-up: we should add an inference-level synthetic that exercises KV cache + model loading + small writes to capture this exact pattern. Putting a draft into the runtime repo PR now.

tariq (eng-infra): rolling rollback started on canaries. I'll monitor for nvme error logs after rollback; if errors persist we escalate vendor/hardware.

maria SRE: thanks all. I'll keep this thread as the main coordination channel. If anyone finds a deterministic repro in lab, paste commands/logs here. For now, mitigation summary: scheduler noop + reduced dirty ratios + route to stable pools + rollback canaries.

jen (support): putting a summary in the customer-facing incident page and tagging affected orgs.

alex (eng-runtime): quick config snippet I'm pushing for the routing fallback (for on-call reference):

```
# fallback rule
- match: {product: hosted-api, tier: latency_sensitive}
  action: prefer(pool=stable-6.4, fallback_model=tiny)
  trigger: p99_ms > 500 for 3 consecutive minutes
```

maria SRE: closing loop for now — p99 on canaries reduced to acceptable levels after rollback and scheduler change. Leaving the rollout paused until infra + firmware team signs off. Will file an incident postmortem and include proposed playbook changes. :white_check_mark:
